tldr: The finite-grid cross-fitted ACW maximizer of transported right-censored RMST has a pointwise Chernoff cutoff law on a strict compact scalar law subclass with centered actual-fold conditions. Its computable leading covariance comes from the censored source score; target-sampling noise cancels at the benefit crossing. A second headline is a maximal continuous-drift obstruction: every deterministic continuous \(\Gamma\) with \(\Gamma(0)=0\) occurs at one anchor-admissible law despite the global unequal-rate nuisance-product benchmark. Thus global products alone cannot imply a centered cutoff law in the larger represented Zhao--Josse--Yang structural class. Feasible Chernoff calibration is pointwise. A separate data-only conservative interval has uniform coverage at least ninety percent and \(O(n^{-1/3})\) worst-case expected length on prespecified collections satisfying the uniform fit event. Whenever the same fitting family is centered at one member, that length rate is matched among covering intervals constrained to contain this nonsmoothed ACW maximizer. The deterministic compact-uniform catalogue is exactly \(\{\Gamma\in C(\mathbb R):\Gamma(0)=0\}\); discontinuous drifts are excluded, and global argmax behavior for arbitrary continuous tails is outside the result.
gap: Zhao, Josse, and Yang prove cube-root tightness for their transported right-censored regime parameter and a central limit theorem for the achieved value, but they do not characterize the cutoff distribution or provide cutoff intervals. Uncensored argmax papers do not calculate the survival martingale covariance, transport normalization, target-noise cancellation, or critical nuisance drift of this estimator.
